<!-- GENERATED by scripts/compile-contracts.mjs from contracts/rules. Edit the rule files, then run npm run contracts:compile. -->

- **invariant** `model/pool-graphic-airs-layer-number-carried`: A pool graphic airs on a LAYER NUMBER carried on its own entry and read through `graphicLayer`, NEVER on one derived from its position in the pool: the hosted control page, the show export, the graphics pack and the production page all read that number. Two entries sharing a layer replace each other on air, which is why the production page warns about a clash rather than silently reordering.
- **rule** `model/production-unit-user-word-production-never`: `shows.ts` is the PRODUCTION unit - the user's word is production, never the old rundown: a name-keyed graphic POOL with one renderer instance each, plus the CUE rundown, where `cues` are additive-optional data rows over the pool and many cues can point at one graphic. Every pool graphic holds its OWN on-air cue, so several are live at once. Packet conventions apply: updatedAt last-write-wins, tombstones.
- **rule** `model/replacing-pool-graphic-name-keeps-entry`: Replacing a pool graphic by name KEEPS the entry's id, because cues reference it through `ShowCue.sourceId` and an id churn would orphan every cue on that graphic. A sync CONFLICT COPY strips the published capabilities and the pin point - the hosted, output, join and presenter slugs and `publishedAt` - so a conflict can never bring a second copy of a live production on air.
- **rule** `model/show-record-carries-production-data-seed`: A show record carries the production-data SEED (`data`) and the field BINDINGS (`bindings`), both additive optional. The LIVE tree is deliberately NOT on this record - see `productionState.ts` for why - and `data` is written by one deliberate authoring act, never per tick.
